title: Patate al Rosmarino
subtitle: Italian roast potatoes with rosemary and garlic
excerpt: Patate al rosmarino are the Italian version of roast potatoes: waxy potato chunks or wedges roasted with olive oil, whole garlic cloves, and fresh rosemary until golden and crisp on the outside and fluffy inside. The method is slightly different from British roast potatoes: no parboiling, less fat, longer roasting: and the result is lighter, more fragrant, and less crisp.
sourceNotes: Patate al rosmarino is one of the most universally eaten dishes in Italian home cooking, appearing across every region. The combination of potato, rosemary, garlic, and olive oil is a cornerstone of Italian roasting. The method uses olive oil rather than animal fat and typically does not parboil the potatoes: a key difference from British roast potatoes.

content.text: Patate al rosmarino are roasted raw, not parboiled first. This gives a denser interior than a British roast potato but a crisp outside when the heat is high enough. Use waxy potatoes rather than floury ones. Floury potatoes break apart rather than hold their shape. The garlic roasts alongside until sweet. It is part of the dish, not just added for flavour.

items.prepNote: waxy or all-purpose, peeled or skin-on, cut into 3 to 4 cm chunks
leaves stripped (or leave whole and pick off at serving)

content.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Place the potato chunks in a large bowl. Add the smashed garlic, rosemary, and olive oil. Season generously with salt and pepper. Toss until every piece is well coated.
Spread onto a large baking tray in a single layer: no overlapping. If the potatoes are crowded, use two trays. Crowded potatoes steam rather than roast.
Roast for 45 to 50 minutes, turning once halfway through, until deeply golden and crisp on the outside and tender when tested with a knife. The garlic should be very soft and slightly caramelised.

items.symptom: Potatoes are pale and soft rather than golden and crisp
items.fix: Use a large tray with room between each piece. If necessary, use two trays. The oven heat must circulate around each piece.

items.symptom: Rosemary burns before the potatoes are done
items.cause: Rosemary leaves were too exposed on the surface and on a very hot tray
items.fix: Add the rosemary after the first 25 minutes, when the potatoes are already golden and the tray has mellowed slightly.

items.cause: Not enough olive oil, or the tray wasn't hot enough when the potatoes went on
items.fix: Use a non-stick tray or line with baking paper. Make sure the potatoes are well coated in olive oil before roasting.

content.text: Patate al rosmarino is the standard potato dish across Italy. It goes alongside roasted meats and grilled fish, or is eaten as a side dish on its own. The method is simpler than a British roast potato: no parboiling, no lard, no coating. The rosemary and garlic give it a fragrance that the plainer British version often lacks.
